clue.text: A good judge of a musical instrument?

definitions.meaning: in England a ... is a barrister or solicitor who sits as a part-time judge in the Crown Court
a wooden woodwind pipe blown at the end, often learnt at school

explanation.surface: A question about who can best appraise an instrument's quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a connoisseur of instruments; in fact the clue gives two separate meanings of one word, the legal office and the woodwind pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a part-time English criminal judge and the end-blown flute.

clue.text: Advised of drink found hidden in the tall grass

indicators.note: the drink is concealed inside the tall grass, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Being told about a bottle concealed among tall plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden in' is the container signal here, not a hidden-word one; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one was advised of has been told or related, which is to have been announced.

clue.text: Shoddy dealer about to load up lift

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
to heap is to pile or load up
to jack up a car is to lift it

explanation.surface: A dishonest trader about to fill an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: Lift looks like an elevator; it is a verb, to jack. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of cheap and inferior goods is a hawker, a shoddy dealer.

clue.text: Gas with a painter fellow

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college

explanation.surface: Chatter with an artistic man.
explanation.walkthrough: Gas looks like a verb, to chatter; it is the noun. 'with a' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A radioactive noble element that is a gas at room temperature.

clue.text: - bound in with the triumphant sea" (Richard II)

definitions.text: - bound in with the triumphant sea" (Richard II)

parts.words: - bound in with the triumphant sea" (Richard II)
parts.note: a gap to fill from John of Gaunt's speech in Shakespeare's Richard II, naming the country girded by the sea

explanation.surface: A line of Shakespeare missing its first word.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the dash stands for the missing word, from Gaunt's 'this sceptred isle' speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaunt's speech names his country, praised as an island kingdom surrounded by the sea.

clue.text: Slough, where gold is stored in quantity

indicators.note: gold is kept inside the word for quantity, so these words signal one piece placed within another

parts.note: a mass is a large quantity
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A description of a hoard of gold kept in bulk, as at a bank in the town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the English town west of London; here it is a bog. 'stored in' signals one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or mire, the same as a marshy bog.

clue.text: Breaks prove a tie for the manual worker

indicators.note: the words prove a tie are broken apart and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Breaking a tied match at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory hand doing physical labour is a mechanic or worker.

clue.text: Mimicking a high-pitched sound

parts.note: a ping is a short high ringing sound

explanation.surface: Imitating a shrill noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying someone the way a monkey would is imitating them.

clue.text: Mounted soldiers clear the ring

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
net means clear after deductions, as net profit

explanation.surface: Cavalry clearing the arena.
explanation.walkthrough: Mounted soldiers suggests cavalry; 'Mounted' turns GIS upwards to SIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal set in a finger ring is a kind of ring.

clue.text: He does like to talk, and that's right in a father

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right goes inside the word for a father

parts.note: pater is Latin, and public-school slang, for father

explanation.surface: A dad who enjoys chatting, and rightly so.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside PATER after its PA; 'and that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who chatters idly is a talker, someone who likes to talk.

clue.text: Quietly go ahead and appeal

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly
to lead is to go in front of others

explanation.surface: Advice to step forward softly and make a request.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to make an earnest request, a verb synonym of appeal.

clue.text: Down-to earth activity which is growing

definitions.text: Down-to earth activity which is growing

parts.words: Down-to earth activity which is growing
parts.note: read literally, a pastime carried out down in the soil, whose whole purpose is making plants grow

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth hobby that is becoming more popular.
explanation.walkthrough: Down-to-earth usually means practical and growing usually means increasing; here they mean working in soil and raising plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Tending plants in soil is the hobby of cultivating a plot.

clue.text: Rueful about restricted social worker

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
pent means shut in or confined, as in pent-up
the ant is the classic social insect that works for its colony

explanation.surface: Someone sorry about a social worker whose powers have been curbed.
explanation.walkthrough: Social worker suggests a council employee; in crosswords it is often the ant, a colony insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling rueful is feeling sorry for what one has done, which is to be contrite.

clue.text: The view taken of fish

definitions.meaning: a point of view or slant on a subject
to fish with a rod and line

explanation.surface: A question of what someone thinks about fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A slant on a story is one sense, and fishing with a hook is the other.

clue.text: Slipped away, pleased to break off

indicators.note: the word pleased is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone happy to end a relationship who then quietly left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break off' signals an anagram of PLEASED; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has slipped away has passed by, so it has gone.

clue.text: Sneering racialist agitation

indicators.note: the word racialist is stirred up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Contempt for stirring up racist feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking through ridicule is a sneering, sarcastic manner.

clue.text: Fruit is gathered in the fall

indicators.note: the word is is collected inside the word for the fall, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: rain is what falls from the sky
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fruit harvested in autumn, the American fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The fall suggests autumn, the harvest season; it is what falls from clouds. 'gathered in' signals one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Only in hotel and church is disrespect apparent

indicators.note: only goes inside hotel, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
sole means only, as in sole survivor
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Rudeness that shows only at a hotel and a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals one piece inside another; 'and', 'is' and 'apparent' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude cheek is a lack of respect, which is disrespect.

clue.text: Those responsible for actors' clothing or furniture

definitions.meaning: theatre staff who help performers into costume
kitchen cabinets with shelves for crockery

explanation.surface: Theatre wardrobe staff, or the cupboards they use.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre helpers who costume performers, and sideboards with shelves for plates.

clue.text: Some fans ask a terrific lot of a sportsman

indicators.note: only some of the letters in these words are used, a run within them

explanation.surface: Fans asking a lot of a star athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'aSK A TERrific'; 'fans' and 'lot of' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: One who races or performs on ice is an athlete, a sportsman.

clue.text: Look after stuff and maintain in good order

explanation.surface: A housekeeping instruction to care for possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixing broken things, and also the state of being well kept.

clue.text: He composed "Sir Patrick and the King"

parts.note: Sir Patrick Spens is the hero of a famous Scottish ballad
ER, Edwardus Rex, is the cipher of a King Edward

explanation.surface: The authorship of a ballad title pairing a knight with a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Patrick Spens is a traditional Scottish ballad. The answer is Edmund Spenser, the Elizabethan poet of The Faerie Queene, who did not write it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan poet wrote verse, so he is one who composed.

clue.text: It's not customary for a holy man to travel widely

parts.note: ST is short for saint
to range is to roam over a wide area

explanation.surface: Wandering is unusual for a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'for a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusual or odd is not customary.

clue.text: One who knows his onions parking a vehicle in the street

indicators.note: the street holds the van parked within it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An expert leaving a van on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knows his onions' is an idiom meaning to be an expert. 'parking' puts the vehicle inside the street; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned scholar is an expert who knows a subject thoroughly.

clue.text: One publicising a laundry aid

definitions.meaning: one who airs views, putting them before the public
a rack or frame on which washed clothes are dried

explanation.surface: An advertiser promoting a washing product.
explanation.definitionFit: One who broadcasts opinions, and also a clothes-drying rack.

clue.text: Strip firing mechanism

definitions.meaning: to ransack and plunder, stripping a place of valuables

explanation.surface: Dismantling a gun's working parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack thoroughly, and a long-barrelled firearm.

clue.text: Relics apt to be smashed into tiny fragments

indicators.note: the words relics apt are broken up and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Ancient relics liable to shatter into bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute bits of matter are specks, very small fragments.

clue.text: Perfect ladies endlessly making changes

indicators.note: the letters left are rearranged, a change of order
the word ladies loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Women forever altering things to make them just right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the S of LADIES, and 'making changes' rearranges LADIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawless is a model of excellence, perfect.

clue.text: Disease causing tenderness

definitions.meaning: an ... in older medical usage is an ailment or disorder
fond feeling or warmth towards someone

explanation.surface: An illness that makes a part of the body sore.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads tenderness as soreness; it is fondness, and the illness sense is old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondness is the everyday sense; an ailment is the older medical one.

clue.text: His is a name in Ireland that is coming back

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name goes inside the turned word for Ireland
the Irish name for Ireland is read from end to start

parts.note: Eire is the Irish-language name of Ireland

explanation.surface: A man whose name returns to Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns EIRE into ERIE, and 'in' puts N inside it. The definition 'His' stands loosely for a man, this being his name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's first name, a pet form of Ernest.

clue.text: A singer in a trio?

definitions.meaning: a boy soprano who sings the highest part

explanation.surface: A question about a vocalist in a three-piece group.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy soprano is one sense; threefold, as of three things, is the other.

clue.text: Flat-foot having to tip a smaller amount

definitions.note: a noun-looking phrase standing for the adjective, describing a foot with no raised back

parts.note: a ship heels when it tips over to one side
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: A policeman, a flatfoot, obliged to give a smaller tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat-foot is slang for a police officer; here it means a shoe or foot that is flat, without a raised back. 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe without a raised back part sits flat, describing a flat foot.
